newsitem.title: INDIA: India call slightly down, gilts lose in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: India call slightly down, gilts lose in thin trade.

text.p: Indian call money ended Friday at 7.25-7.75 percent, marginally down from opening quotes of 7.75-8.0 percent, dealers said.

They said most of the day's trade was done at rates close to 8.0 percent. "Rates continue to remain higher than market expectations," said a dealer at a foreign bank. "Most market players had expected call money to drift down to around 6.0 percent by close, given fairly good inflows of around eight billion rupees from interest payments on government securities this week."
"But lenders are keeping rates high," he said. "There was also enough demand for funds today to keep rates above 7.5 percent throughout the day."
Dealers said prices of government securities were slightly down in light trade. Most of the trades on Friday were in securities with maturities up to 1999, they said.

"Trade is poor at the moment as call money is higher than expected," said a dealer. "There was some selling pressure but nothing major really happened. Market players are waiting for call money to come down or for a fresh government bond issue announcement before taking positions."

The 13.50 percent 1997 government stock dropped to 101.70 rupees from its last traded 101.93, the 13.70 percent 1999 to 104.85 from 104.90, the 13.85 percent 2000 to 105.45 from 105.62 and the 12.69 percent 2002 to 100.17 from 100.21, dealers said.

Among treasury bills, the bill maturing in January 1998 was traded at a yield of 9.35 percent against last yield of 9.3, October 1997 bills at 8.8 percent against 8.87 and September bills at 8.5 percent against 8.65, dealers said.
